regulation.name: Resolução CVM 175
regulation.instrument: FIDC — fundo de investimento em direitos creditórios
regulation.note: Engineering intent, not legal advice. The mapping below is the subset a token can enforce; everything else lives in the fund's documents and its administrator.

identity.comment: The qualitative half: who may hold. Enforced on every token operation via velum-policy, which asks the RWA identity verifier. IMPORTANT: a claim topic only takes effect when at least one trusted issuer is registered FOR THAT TOPIC. Registering the topic alone is a silent no-op — verify_identity iterates (topic, issuers) pairs and skips a topic whose issuer list is empty, with no error. Always pair a topic with its issuers here and on-chain.

claim_topics.name: kyc
claim_topics.comment: Identity established by an approved certifier. Without it the account cannot register, deposit, transfer or withdraw.

claim_topics.name: qualified_investor
claim_topics.comment: Investidor qualificado under CVM 175. Declared, not active: neither the topic nor an issuer for it is registered in the deployed registry. VERIFIED that turning it on works — with topic 2 registered AND the issuer trusted for it, a holder carrying only topic 1 flipped to is_authorized=false; with the topic registered but NO issuer, the same holder stayed authorized. State restored afterwards.

trusted_issuers.comment: Address supplied at deploy time; in production the fund's KYC provider or its administrator. Its topic set is what makes a topic bite — see the warning above.

quantitative.comment: The half the policy interface cannot express, because balances are commitments. Enforced by holder-attested proofs instead — see velum-attest.

minimum_position.comment: The holder proves position >= this value and a contract records it. Note the distinction: this is ATTESTABLE, not enforced — nothing compels a holder to attest, and no operation is blocked for lack of an attestation. A consumer (transfer agent, distributor, another contract) decides what to require. Enforcing it inside the transfer would need the quantitative rule in the circuit itself — see experiments/circuit-cap-poc. Also note this is the ticket floor, not the CVM net-worth test for investidor qualificado, which is an identity claim (topic 2) attested off-chain.

concentration_ceiling.comment: Same construction with the predicate inverted, provable against a public fund total. Circuit not built.

subordination_ratio.comment: Senior/subordinated ratio is a statement over encrypted aggregates ACROSS accounts. Open problem — see whitepaper §6.

freeze.comment: Immediate and unilateral, inherited from the confidential token's compliance extension. Verified: freeze(alice) emitted Frozen and her next policy-gated operation failed with #3601 AccountFrozen — distinguishable from #3602 NotAuthorizedByPolicy. unfreeze restored it.

sac_passthrough.comment: Configured (the deployment event records sac_passthrough: true) but its EFFECT is untestable on this deployment: the underlying is the native XLM SAC, which has no admin and whose authorized() is always true, so there is no issuer able to deauthorize an account. Exercising the cascade needs an underlying with a real issuer — e.g. the fund's own classic asset with AUTH_REVOCABLE. Marked unverified rather than assumed.

clawback.comment: Not available: once value enters the wrapper the SEP-41 ledger lists the contract as holder. Design and circuit exist (whitepaper §11, circuits/seize); the migration does not. Freeze is the control that works today.

deployment.comment: Testnet only. The UltraHonk verifier upstream is developer preview and unaudited; do not point this profile at mainnet.
